question: A mortgage rate goes from 2% to 3%, reported as up one point. By how much does the yearly interest bill rise?
answer: About 50%. On a €200,000 loan, interest at 2% costs €4,000 a year; at 3% it costs €6,000. The rate moved one percentage point, a step on its scale, but the bill grew by half of itself: €2,000 more every year, behind a headline that sounded like a rounding error.
move: When a rate moves by points, work out what happens to the bill.
ask: When a rate I pay rises by one point, do I know what that adds to my bill?
trap: About 1%, reading a one-point rise as a one-percent rise.
reference: Paulos, Innumeracy: Mathematical Illiteracy and Its Consequences, Hill and Wang, 1988
